subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on a node host connected to a non-loopback gateway fail closed before starting provider auth, or should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned credential sync/forwarding path?
rationale: Both options change a credential boundary: fail-closed behavior is safer and smaller but changes an existing CLI flow, while gateway sync is more convenient but needs a deliberate API/security design for moving OAuth credentials across hosts.

options.title: Fail closed on remote node hosts
options.body: Block auth login before OAuth or token creation when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway, and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Keep the issue open for a reviewed gateway-owned credential sync API instead of adding ad hoc profile copying from the node host.

options.title: Accept current local writes
options.body: Close as not planned only if maintainers intentionally accept that node-host auth login affects the node-local store rather than the gateway credential owner.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on remote node hosts
recommendation.body: Block auth login before OAuth or token creation when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway, and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest current routing signal from recent auth CLI history and prior maintainer follow-up on the linked remote-node auth guard PRs.
